Tinsley was unable to win a spot on the Bengals' roster coming out of training camp, but he could have a clearer path to seeing playing time in Houston at some point in 2026 with Jayden Higgins (knee) out for the season and Tank Dell (knee) set to miss at least the team's first four games.

items.headline: The Texans signed Whittington to their practice squad Monday.
items.summary: After signing with the Texans in May as an undrafted rookie out of Oregon, Whittington took part in training camp and the preseason, but was unable to secure a spot on the final roster heading into Week 1. Though Whittington will stick around in the organization, Jawhar Jordan will likely rank as the Texans' preferred choice to elevate to the roster if the team's depth in the backfield gets tested at any point.

items.headline: Downs caught two of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 41-23 loss to the Ravens.
items.summary: Downs' four targets tied Jonathan Taylor for fourth on the team behind Alec Pierce (six), Keenan Allen (six) and Tyler Warren (five), but it was notable that Downs led the team with 32 routes on Daniel Jones' 34 dropbacks. He was in the slot 78.8 percent of the time, and his 93.8 percent route participation suggests Downs is an every-down wideout this season after playing behind both Michael Pittman and Pierce in previous seasons. Downs should have better days moving forward and gets a Week 2 date with the Chiefs next Sunday.

items.headline: Giddens (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.summary: Giddens missed a big chunk of training camp and the preseason due to a hamstring injury, and he was passed on the depth chart by rookie Seth McGowan as the RB2 behind workhorse back Jonathan Taylor.

items.headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive as the Colts' emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
items.summary: Leonard lost out on the QB2 job to Anthony Richardson behind Daniel Jones over the summer. Across five regular-season appearances last season, Leonard completed just 58.2 percent of his 67 pass attempts for 415 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions, averaging a subpar 6.2 yards per attempt.

items.headline: Ogletree (neck) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
items.summary: The tight end was limited by a neck injury a day earlier. Ogletree is trending toward playing in Sunday's opener against Baltimore. The 2022 sixth-round pick has added depth to the Colts' tight-end spot throughout his career, seeing action on special teams as well.

items.headline: Colts WR Allen relinquishes No. 13 to teammate Treadwell
items.summary: Receiver Keenan Allen will wear No. 10 with the Colts this season, marking the first time in his 13-year NFL career that he will not be wearing No. 13, which will be worn by Laquon Treadwell.

items.headline: Mallory (thumb) was placed on injured reserve by the Colts on Sunday with a designation to return, JJ Stankevitz of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Mallory suffered a thumb injury, and he sat out the team's last two games of the preseason. The tight end will now be forced to miss at least four contests to open the 2026 campaign, and the earliest he'll be able to make his regular-season debut is in Week 5 against the Steelers on Oct. 11.

items.headline: Montgomery (abdomen) was placed on injured reserve by the Colts on Sunday, JJ Stankevitz of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Montgomery signed with the team in early August, ultimately reeling in two of three targets for 21 yards during the preseason. The wide receiver appears to have picked up an abdominal injury at some point during the preseason, and he is now set to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR, unless he reaches an injury settlement with Indianapolis.

items.headline: The Colts cut Bentley from the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Bentley signed to the Colts' practice squad Monday after being waived by the team Sunday following the conclusion of training camp. He's been let go by the team for the second time in three days and will look to join an organization in need of backfield depth.

items.headline: The Colts signed Booth to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Booth failed to make the Browns' 53-man roster at the end of training camp, but he'll get a new opportunity with the Colts as a member of the team's practice squad. Across three preseason games with Cleveland, Booth turned 17 carries into 109 yards and a touchdown while adding three catches (on four targets) for minus-three yards and two kickoff returns for 54 yards.

items.headline: Brown was signed to the Colts practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Brown didn't make the Colts' 53-man roster but will at least remain with the team as a member of the practice squad. The 32-year-old has an extensive NFL resume, suiting up for the Browns, Texans, Patriots, Seahawks and Cardinals throughout his career and catching 74 passes for 752 yards and three touchdowns across 92 regular-season games.

items.headline: The Colts signed Castle to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie out of Duke failed to make the Colts' 53-man roster but did enough to receive an invitation to the team's practice squad. He logged 18 carries for 88 yards across the Colts' three preseason games and would be a candidate for elevation to the active roster if one of Jonathan Taylor, Seth McGowan or DJ Giddens were to miss time.

items.headline: Fletcher was signed to the Colts' practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Fletcher was cut by the Buccaneers on Aug. 29 after signing with the team as an undrafted free agent in May. The tight end will now have an opportunity to operate as an extreme depth option behind Tyler Warren with Indianapolis.

items.headline: The Colts signed Gould (groin) to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Gould appeared in 19 regular-season games for the Colts since the team drafted him in the fifth round of the 2024 NFL Draft. While the 25-year-old is on the practice squad for now, his versatility could earn him more opportunities moving forward.

items.headline: Westbrook-Ikhine was signed to the Colts' practice squad Monday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Westbrook-Ikhine was let go by the team Sunday, but he'll remain in Indianapolis ahead of the regular season. With Alec Pierce (ankle) still uncertain for Week 1, it's possible that Westbrook-Ikhine will be elevated to the active roster for the team's matchup with the Ravens on Sunday, Sept. 13.

items.headline: Abdullah earned a spot on the Jaguars' 53-man roster following a strong training camp, John Oehser of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Abdullah and LeQuint Allen (undisclosed) will enter the regular season as the rotational running backs behind co-starters Bhayshul Tuten (illness) and Chris Rodriguez. Abdullah played in only one of the Jaguars' three preseason games, but he did enough during training camp and joint practices to crack the 53-man roster for the 2026 campaign. The 2015 second-rounder appeared in 13 regular-season games for the Colts last year, finishing with 14 carries for 60 yards and a touchdown along with 16 catches (on 17 targets) for 99 yards.

items.headline: Who keeps the ball? Trevor Lawrence's 100th TD is rookie's first catch
items.summary: Trevor Lawrence's 100th NFL touchdown pass went to rookie wide receiver Josh Cameron, who hauled it in for his first NFL catch.

items.headline: Ewers (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
items.summary: The Jaguars traded for Ewers toward the tail end of training camp, but the 2025 seventh-rounder will be a healthy scratch Week 1 while Nick Mullens serves as Jacksonville's backup QB behind Trevor Lawrence. Ewers isn't listed as the emergency third quarterback against Cleveland, so his next chance to suit up is Week 2 against Denver on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: Koziol (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
items.summary: Koziol, the Jaguars' fifth-round pick of the 2026 NFL Draft, will be a healthy inactive for Week 1, so his next chance to make his regular-season debut is Week 2 against the Broncos on Sunday, Sept. 20. Brenton Strange, Quintin Morris and rookie second-rounder Nate Boerkircher will be Jacksonville's active tight ends against Cleveland.

items.headline: The Jaguars elevated Mullens from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: Mullens will likely serve as the emergency No. 3 quarterback if Trevor Lawrence and Quinn Ewers both go down in Sunday's game against the Browns. Mullens will be eligible for only two more practice squad elevations this regular season, so this is not a role the quarterback can fill perpetually.

items.headline: Rodriguez rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-10 win over the Browns.
items.summary: Bhayshul Tuten got the start in the backfield and out-snapped Rodriguez 28 to 23 and out-carried him 15 to six in one of the friendliest rushing environments the Jaguars will see all season after Jacksonville jumped out to a 31-0 lead early in the third quarter. The lack of volume and production from Rodriguez in this spot is concerning for his fantasy viability moving forward, as Tuten seemed to have the clear upper hand and averaged 4.4 yards per carry to Rodriguez's 3.8 mark. Tuten also caught a 22-yard pass, while Rodriguez didn't see a target. It was clear against Cleveland that Tuten is the preferred fantasy option in this backfield.

items.headline: Week 1 winners and losers: Caleb Williams and Josh Allen dominate; Ja'Marr Chase disappoints
items.summary: Caleb Williams, Josh Allen and Trevor Lawrence came up big in Week 1, while Ja'Marr Chase, Drake London and Colston Loveland had very quiet days.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Aguilar to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Jaguars waived Aguilar during Sunday's cut-down day. The quarterback played in all three preseason games, completing 17 of his 20 pass attempts for 230 yards and a touchdown. The 25-year-old cleared waivers and will now compete with Nick Mullens on the practice squad for a chance to be elevated to the active roster if Trevor Lawrence or Quinn Ewers suffer an injury.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Jones to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Jaguars released Jones during Sunday's cut-down day, but the 28-year-old did enough to receive an invitation to the practice squad. The veteran wide receiver participated in all three preseason contests, catching his sole target for five yards.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Pena to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Jaguars waived Pena during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers but did enough during training camp to receive an invite back to the team's practice squad. The undrafted free agent out of Penn State caught 10 of his 14 targets for 149 yards and a touchdown over three preseason games.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Rucci to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: The Colts waived Rucci during Sunday's cut-down day. The tight end now catches on with the Jaguars' practice squad. Rucci played in four regular-season games for the Dolphins during the 2025 season, logging 81 total snaps.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Taylor to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Jaguars waived Taylor during Sunday's cut-down day. The running back cleared waivers and was proficient enough during training camp to receive an invitation to the team's practice squad. The undrafted free agent out of Virginia participated in all three preseason games, rushing 38 times for 125 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Trammell to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Trammell was released by the Jaguars during Sunday's cut-down day but did enough during training camp to receive an invitation to the practice squad. The wide receiver participated in all three preseason games, catching six passes for 59 yards.

items.headline: The Jaguars signed Wortham to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Jaguars waived Wortham during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and has returned to the team. The undrafted free agent out of Montana participated in all three preseason games, catching seven of his eight targets for 97 yards.

items.headline: Allen is listed as a backup receiver on Kansas City's unofficial depth chart ahead of Monday's season opener versus the Broncos, Charles Goldsmith of AtoZSports.com reports.
items.summary: A rookie fifth-round pick out of Cincinnati, Allen generated plenty of positive buzz in training camp and the preseason, but he doesn't appear to have a path to meaningful playing time heading into Week 1. Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy are locked in as the clear top two options on the depth chart, but Allen could eventually push Tyquan Thornton for the No. 3 spot. Thornton possesses more speed of the two and found some success as a vertical threat in Andy Reid's scheme last season, but Allen offers a more diverse route tree and could be a higher-volume target earner if Rice or Worthy were to miss time.

items.headline: Johnson is in line to be Kenneth Walker's backup for the Chiefs this season.
items.summary: The Chiefs had final roster cutdowns Sunday and waived veteran Emari Demercado, clearing a path to a role for Johnson. The rookie out of Nebraska impressed throughout training camp and the preseason. Kansas City also has Brashard Smith on the roster, but Johnson may be the handcuff to target for fantasy managers.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Odukoya to the practice squad Sunday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Odukoya is from the Netherlands and joined the NFL through the International Player Pathway Program. The tight end had a tryout with the Chiefs last Friday and will now provide depth for legendary teammate Travis Kelce on the practice squad. Odukoya played in three games for the Titans in 2024, logging 36 total snaps.

items.headline: Smith is the third and final running back on the Chiefs' 53-man roster for the 2026 regular season, Matt McMullen of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Smith and Emari Demercado entered training camp battling for a depth spot on the Chiefs' active roster, but the former ended up winning that RB3 role behind Kenneth Walker and rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson. Smith, a 2025 seventh-rounder, played in all 17 regular-season games in his rookie campaign, turning 44 carries into 151 yards (3.4 YPC) while catching 25 passes (on 35 targets) for 172 yards and a touchdown. Walker figures to be the bellcow running back for the Chiefs, but Smith could see the field on passing downs to give the former a breather.

items.headline: Holiday (undisclosed) was placed on injured reserve by the Chiefs on Sunday.
items.summary: Holiday is dealing with an undisclosed injury, and he did not play during the preseason. The wide receiver will now be forced to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR, unless he is able to reach an injury settlement with Kansas City.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Armstrong to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Armstrong was waived by the Chiefs on Sunday but will remain with the team as a member of the practice squad. The 25-year-old appeared in three preseason games for Kansas City in 2026, totaling seven catches for 85 yards.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Carter to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Carter was in the mix for the Falcons' RB3 role, but Atlanta ended up keeping only two healthy running backs -- Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson -- on the 53-man roster, with Trey Sermon (undisclosed) on season-ending injured reserve. Carter will get a new opportunity with the Chiefs and would be a candidate for elevation to the team's active roster if one of Kenneth Walker (ankle), Emmett Johnson or Brashard Smith were to miss time. Carter appeared in seven regular-season games for the Falcons last year, logging nine carries for 60 yards while also contributing on special teams.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Evans to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Evans didn't make the Chiefs' 53-man roster but will stay with the team as a member of the practice squad. He went undrafted in 2026 after spending his final collegiate season at Washington in 2025, totaling 17 catches for 254 yards and one touchdown across 11 regular-season games.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed Ott to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Ott joined the Chiefs on May 1 as an undrafted free agent and played in all three of the team's preseason games. He was waived Sunday after failing to crack the 53-man roster, but Ott will stay in Kansas City on the practice squad. The Oklahoma product would be a top candidate for elevation to the active roster if the Chiefs require additional depth in the backfield.

items.headline: Laube made the Raiders' 53-man roster at the end of training camp and could operate in an elevated role on offense against the Dolphins in Week 1 if Ashton Jeanty (ankle) is limited or ruled out.
items.summary: Jeanty suffered a low-ankle sprain during the Raiders' training camp practice Aug. 23. The relief for the Raiders was that it wasn't a high-ankle sprain or worse, and although there's optimism around Jeanty playing Week 1, the injury could limit his effectiveness and playing time. That would open the door for both Mike Washington and Laube to operate in expanded roles on offense, with the latter also seeing the field on special teams as a kickoff returner.

items.headline: The Raiders elevated Myarick from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: With Brock Bowers (knee) set to miss a couple of weeks as he recovers from meniscus surgery, Myrarick will have a chance to prove his worth on an NFL field. The tight end is set for the No. 3 role behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas, likely playing most of his snaps for the Raiders' special teams unit.

items.headline: O'Connell (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Raiders' emergency third quarterback against the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: Kirk Cousins beat out first-overall pick Fernando Mendoza for the starting quarterback job Week 1, so O'Connell will suit up as the emergency QB3. As such, O'Connell is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Cousins and Mendoza were to leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Tucker caught two of four targets for 27 yards in a 27-13 win against Miami on Sunday.
items.summary: Tucker had a relatively quiet performance, though that was the case for the Raiders' wideout corps as a whole, as no WR exceeded Tucker's 27 receiving yards. Instead, RB Ashton Jeanty (6-45-2 receiving line) and TE Michael Mayer (6-32-0) featured as Las Vegas' top pass catchers, while the offense ran primarily on the ground through Jeanty (23-102-0 rushing line) and Mike Washington Jr. (7-41-0). The Raiders don't figure to play ahead as often this season as they did Sunday, so the team may need its wideouts more often moving forward, though start tight end Brock Bowers (knee) could return to action as soon as next week and eventually figures to command the greatest share of QB Kirk Cousins' attention. Las Vegas seems likely to face a tougher challenge in Week 2 against the Chargers.

items.headline: Washington rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Raiders' 27-13 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: After Ashton Jeanty dealt with an ankle sprain for the previous month, it was unclear if the Raiders would dial things back with their star running back. Jeanty went on to handle a full workload, rushing 23 times for 102 yards, while also leading the team in catches and receiving yards with a 6-45-2 line. Washington looked good on his seven chances, but it's clear Jeanty is healthy, making Washington a mere bench stash in fantasy.

items.headline: The Raiders elevated White from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: White is set to suit up for the Raiders because the team has three wide receivers currently on injured reserve. Dont'e Thornton (undisclosed), Justin Shorter (undisclosed) and Corey Rucker (undisclosed) all must miss at least four games, allowing White to show out as a valuable depth option for the receiving corps and special teams unit.

items.headline: Runyon (undisclosed) was placed on injured reserve by the Raiders on Sunday with a designation to return.
items.summary: Runyon did not play in the preseason, and he's dealing with an undisclosed injury ahead of the 2026 campaign. The tight end will be forced to miss at least four contests to open the regular season, and the earliest he could return to action is Week 5 versus the Patriots on Oct. 11. Runyon was primarily as a special-teams asset in 2025, so his absence won't carry much of an impact on offense.

items.headline: The Raiders placed Thornton (undisclosed) on injured reserve Monday.
items.summary: It's still unclear what is bothering Thornton, but he'll now be required to miss at least the first four games of the regular season. The 2025 fourth-rounder corralled just 10 of 30 targets for 135 scoreless yards across 15 regular-season appearances as a rookie last season and missed the entire preseason this summer. Under a new coaching staff, it's unclear what kind of role Thornton will have this season once healthy.

items.headline: Las Vegas signed Bell to its practice squad Thursday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.summary: Bell was waived by the Saints on Saturday after missing the cut for their 53-man roster, but now he's getting a shot to make an impression with a new team. The Raiders have arguably the most unproven group of wide receivers in the league to start 2026, so if Bell is elevated to the active roster at any point, he could be a candidate to draw targets right away.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Gurd to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Raiders waived Gurd on Aug. 29 ahead of cutdown day. The undrafted free agent out of Cincinnati cleared waivers and will now have a chance to play for the team that originally took a shot on him. Gurd will provide additional depth at tight end from his practice-squad spot.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Hemby to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Hemby joined the Raiders in late April as an undrafted free agent and entered training camp as a long shot to make the 53-man roster. Across three preseason games, he logged 11 carries for 38 yards while adding three catches (on as many targets) for 22 yards and 105 yards on four kickoffs. He was waived Sunday after failing to make the active roster, but Hemby seemingly impressed the coaching staff enough to be invited back on the practice squad. There's five wide receivers on the Raiders' 53-man roster, but Hemby would be a candidate for elevation from the practice squad if one of those receivers were to miss time.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Ogunbowale to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Ogunbowale was unable to beat out Dylan Laube for the Raiders' RB3 role behind Ashton Jeanty (ankle) and Mike Washington, prompting Las Vegas to release Ogunbowale on Sunday. The veteran running back will stay with the organization as a member of the practice squad, and he could be elevated to the active roster for Week 1 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Sept. 13 if Jeanty is ruled out.

items.headline: The Raiders signed Thompkins to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Thompkins joined the Raiders in late July and appeared in all three preseason games. He logged four catches (on six targets) for 33 yards and contributed on special teams as a returner, recording 25 yards on four punt returns and 198 yards on seven kickoff returns. He was released by the Raiders on Sunday, but Thompkins will stick around on the practice squad and could be elevated to the active roster if the team needs another pass catcher or returner.

items.headline: Harris (undisclosed) is not listed on the Week 1 injury report Wednesday.
items.summary: Harris dealt with an unspecified injury last month but is fine for Sunday's season opener against the Cardinals. He's expected to fill the WR3 role behind Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnson this season, but the Chargers also figure to use plenty of TE-heavy sets with Charlie Kolar, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku.

items.headline: Johnston caught two of his six targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 26-14 loss to the Cardinals.
items.summary: Johnston was unable to capture 66 percent of his targets, failing to show up even after No. 1 wide receiver Ladd McConkey (chest) exited the game with a chest injury. Johnston also took a costly false start penalty in the fourth quarter, which cannot be good for the wide receiver's chemistry with quarterback Justin Herbert.

items.headline: Lambert-Smith (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.summary: Lambert-Smith exited the second half of Sunday's game. If the hamstring issue is anything other than a minor hit the wide receiver will likely be required to miss time as he manages the issue. Derius Davis may see an increased role in the Chargers' passing offense in Lambert-Smith's absence.

items.headline: Mitchell rushed four times for nine yards in a Week 1 loss to Arizona on Sunday. He added 47 yards on two kickoff returns.
items.summary: Mitchell had a long rush of eight yards but combined for just three yards on his other three carries. While he also contributed in the return game, it was a bland Chargers debut for the 24-year-old, who joined Los Angeles as a free agent in March. The Chargers' run game as a whole was largely stifled Sunday, as Omarion Hampton -- the only other RB on the team to log a carry -- finished with a mediocre 43 yards on 12 carries, though he did score a touchdown. Mitchell will look to make more of an impression in Week 2 versus Las Vegas next Sunday.

items.headline: Thompson (hip) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
items.summary: Thompson practiced fully Friday after limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday. The fourth-round rookie wideout is expected to see some action on special teams as a returner and should slot in as the Chargers' fourth receiver behind Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris.

items.headline: The Chargers signed  Desrosiers to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Chargers waived Desrosiers on Sunday. The running back cleared waivers and had a strong enough training camp to be invited to the team's practice squad. The undrafted free agent out of Memphis played in all three preseason games, rushing 23 times for 166 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: The Chargers cut Jennings from the practice squad Monday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Jennings signed with the practice squad Tuesday after being waived from the Chargers' 90-man roster on cutdown day. The wide receiver was cut to make room for cornerback Isas Waxter, who signed with the practice squad in a corresponding move.

items.headline: The Chargers signed  Johnson to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Chargers waived Johnson on Sunday. The running back cleared waivers and was promptly invited back to the team's practice squad. Johnson played in all three preseason games, rushing 15 times for 53 net yards and two touchdowns, adding two receptions for 68 yards. Johnson may have a shot at some regular-season playing time if Keaton Mitchell (undisclosed) misses time.

items.headline: The Chargers signed  Svoboda to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Svoboda cleared waivers after being cut by the Chargers during Sunday's cut-down day. The undrafted free agent out of Wyoming performed well enough throughout training camp that the team extended him an invitation to the practice squad. The tight end played in all three preseason games, catching both of his targets for nine yards.

items.headline: The Chargers signed  Uiagalelei to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Chargers waived Uiagalelei during Sunday's cut-down day. The quarterback cleared waivers and has shown enough potential in training camp to once again be invited to the team's practice squad, similar to his rookie year. Uiagalelei participated in all three preseason contests, completing 24 of his 42 pass attempts for 341 yards and two touchdowns.

items.headline: The Chargers signed Wease to their practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Wease cleared waivers after the Dolphins cut him Saturday but he's now getting a fresh opportunity with a new club. In three games with Miami in 2025, he reeled in six of 10 targets for 139 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: Atwell (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's tilt against the 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Atwell was with the Dolphins during the offseason until the Rams traded for him Aug. 27, though he should be fairly well-versed in the team's playbook after spending each of the past five campaigns with Los Angeles. It seemed Atwell could have a fairly big role in the Dolphins' thin wideout corps, but now that he's back with the Rams, he'll be competing with the likes of Konata Mumpfield, Xavier Smith and Jordan Whittington for playing time (and active status) behind Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. It remains to be seen if Nacua will be suspended by the league at some point; if that were to happen, Atwell could move into a more significant role.

items.headline: Bennett completed two of three passes for 13 yards and rushed once for nine yards in the Rams' 27-7 Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
items.summary: Bennett came into the game for the Rams' last offensive possession once the game was officially out of reach. The quarterback was effective but couldn't produce any points, as he ran out of time after 10 total plays.

items.headline: Corum rushed 10 times for 54 yards and wasn't targeted during the Rams' 27-7 Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Melbourne, Australia.
items.summary: Corum's backfield mate Kyren Williams worked as the starting running back and logged his first carry on the Rams' second play from scrimmage, but Corum garnered his first touch to start Los Angeles' second drive and ripped off a nine-yard run. The third-year pro would go on to outpace Williams by 13 rushing yards on one fewer carry, although Corum's lack of a pass-game role was a disappointment. Nevertheless, it appears preseason talk about an even closer division of labor between the two backs this season could have some credibility as a Week 2 home matchup against the Giants on Monday night, Sept. 21 approaches.

items.headline: Daniels (coach's decision) is a healthy scratch for Thursday's matchup versus San Francisco in Melbourne, Australia, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Daniels was able to make the Rams' 53-man roster with a strong showing during the preseason, but he isn't high enough in the pecking order at this point to be active on gameday.  Los Angeles will roll with Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Xavier Smith as its WR corps Thursday.

items.headline: Ferguson failed to haul in his lone target during the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1.
items.summary: The lone pass Ferguson saw from Matthew Stafford was on fourth-and-5 midway through the fourth quarter, which easily sailed over the second-year tight end and out of bounds. Ferguson's 31 snaps on offense were ahead of Tyler Higbee (12) but behind Colby Parkinson (41), so Ferguson's role in the Rams offense figures to mostly be as a run blocker in 12- and 13-man personnel. The Rams will host the Giants in Week 2 on Monday, Sept. 21.

items.headline: Higbee secured both of his targets for 12 yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1.
items.summary: Higbee played just 12 offensive snaps and ran only five routes on 28 dropbacks by the Rams. He was well behind both Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson in terms of playing time and routes at tight end for Los Angeles. Higbee would need an injury ahead of him to gain fantasy relevance.

items.headline: Klare (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's season-opener versus San Francisco in Melbourne, Australia, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: The Rams liked Klare enough to select him in the second round of the NFL Draft in April, but he's not going to be an option for the team in Week 1. Los Angeles has a crowded tight-end room that includes three veterans in Colby Parkinson, Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen along with second-year pro Terrance Ferguson, so Klare may not log much playing time this year as long as those above him in the pecking order are healthy.

items.headline: Mumpfield did not catch his only target during the Rams' 27-7 loss against the 49ers in Week 1.
items.summary: Mumpfield lined up for 16 of the Rams' 61 offensive snaps in Week 1, and he played six snaps on special teams. As long as two-time Pro Bowler Puka Nacua and veteran Davante Adams are available, there likely won't be room for any other Rams wide receivers to draw many targets.

items.headline: Parkinson caught one pass (on two targets) for six yards during the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1.
items.summary: Parkinson was on the field for 47 of the Rams' 61 offensive plays (77.0 percent), which was ahead of fellow tight ends Terrance Ferguson (31 snaps), Davis Allen (21 snaps, head) and Tyler Higbee (12 snaps). However, Parkinson was unable to convert that extra playing time into offensive production, with the 2020 fourth-rounder being used more as a blocker, with Higbee leading the position group with two catches on as many targets for 12 yards. Parkinson saw an uptick in involvement in the passing game as the 2025 season progressed, but he's off to a slow start to the 2026 campaign. The Rams will make their home debut Week 2 on Monday, Sept. 21 against the Giants, whose defense ranked in the top-10 in fantasy production against tight ends in 2025.

items.headline: Rivers rushed five times for 19 yards and caught one pass for five yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1.
items.summary: With the Rams getting blown out by 20 points in the fourth quarter, Rivers saw eight offensive snaps late in the game and piled up six touches during his minimal playing time. He's the RB3 behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum.

items.headline: Simpson is inactive as the Rams' emergency third quarterback for Thursday's matchup against San Francisco in Melbourne, Australia, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: It thus appears Stetson Bennett has won Los Angeles' No. 2 QB job, at least for the first game of the season. Simpson, who was taken by the Rams in the first round of April's NFL Draft, can make his NFL debut Thursday only if both starter Matthew Stafford and Bennett have to exit due to injury, illness, or ejection.

items.headline: Smith played 16 of 61 offensive snaps in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1 and didn't record any touches or targets.
items.summary: Smith is the Rams' punt returner and returned one for 11 yards. He also gained 25 yards on one kick return. His offensive snaps were elevated late in the game when the Rams pulled their starters. Smith has next to no fantasy value.

items.headline: Whittington caught his lone target for eight yards in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the 49ers in Week 1.
items.summary: Whittington played 25 of 61 offensive snaps but saw his playing time elevated some late in the fourth quarter after the Rams pulled their starters. He also saw 13 snaps on special teams, returning four kicks for 94 yards. Whittington may need some injuries ahead of him to be a useful fantasy asset.

items.headline: The Rams signed Bachman to the practice squad Monday, Zach Edwards of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Bachman was a late addition to the Rams' training camp roster, joining the team Aug. 18. He appeared in two preseason games, logging six catches (on seven targets) for 57 yards while adding two tackles. He was released by the Rams on Sunday after failing to make the 53-man roster, but Bachman did enough to receive an invitation to stay in Los Angeles as a member of the organization's practice squad.

items.headline: The Rams signed Connors to the practice squad Monday, Zach Edwards of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Connors put together a strong preseason, turning 26 carries into 96 yards while adding seven catches on eight targets for 53 yards across three games. He also contributed on special teams with a 25-yard kickoff return and a tackle. It wasn't quite enough for Connors to crack the 53-man roster, but after being waived Sunday, the University of Houston product will stay with the Rams as a member of the team's practice squad. He would be candidate to be elevated to the active roster if one of Kyren Williams, Blake Corum or Ronnie Rivers were to miss time.

items.headline: The Rams signed Presley to the practice squad Monday, Zach Edwards of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Presley was waived by the Rams on Sunday despite a productive preseason, finishing with 14 catches (on 17 targets) for 125 yards and a touchdown while returning two kickoffs for 59 yards and one punt for 11 yards. He's back with the Rams on the practice squad and could be elevated to the active roster if the team needs a pass catcher and special-teams contributor on game day.

items.headline: Villari signed with the Rams' practice squad Monday, Zach Edwards of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Villari was waived by the Rams on Saturday after failing to crack the 53-man roster but he'll stay with the organization as a member of the practice squad. The Rams currently carry five tight ends on the active roster, and Villari could be elevated from the practice squad for Week 1 against the 49ers if either or both of Terrance Ferguson (general soreness) and Davis Allen (quadriceps) were ruled out for the regular-season opener.

items.headline: The Rams signed Waters to the practice squad Monday, Zach Edwards of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Waters was waived by the Rams on Sunday after not making the 53-man roster, but he'll stick around as a member of the team's practice squad. Across three preseason games, Waters turned 30 carries into 140 yards (4.8 YPC) while adding one catch (on two targets) for four yards.

items.headline: Achane rushed 11 times for 36 yards and brought in four of five targets for 30 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: Achane ceded only one carry to backup Jaylen Wright, but the former's opportunities on the ground were limited due to a game script that saw the Dolphins trailing throughout. Achane did finish second in receptions and third in targets for Miami on the afternoon, and his 15 touches were tops among all of the team's skill-position players. He should continue to enjoy a solid floor in terms of his workload each week, as even if the Dolphins are frequently in scenarios similar to Sunday's, his prowess as a receiver projects to consistently keep him on the field.

items.headline: Bell estimated Thursday that his conditioning is back to "80 to 85 percent" following last season's torn ACL, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
items.summary: Bell underwent surgery for a clean tear of his ACL last December and isn't on the injury report for Miami's Week 1 game against the Raiders on Sunday, but the rookie wideout is still working back into game shape. While he won't be on a proverbial pitch count against Las Vegas, there's a chance the Dolphins use multiple receivers with some sort of rotation. Bell is listed as a starter, but he's highly unlikely to run 100 percent of the routes Sunday. He could develop into the team's No. 1 wide receiver by the end of the season.

items.headline: Cook (coach's decision) will be the emergency quarterback for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
items.summary: The Dolphins claimed Cook off waivers from the Jets after cutdown day. The quarterback will sit behind Malik Willis and Kyle McCord, only able to enter the game if both players can no longer participate.

items.headline: Douglas brought in five of seven targets for 94 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: Douglas led the Dolphins in receptions and receiving yards while finishing second in targets in his NFL regular-season debut. The rookie third-round pick tied fellow wideout Malik Washington for a team-long 30-yard catch as well, and Douglas' immediate chemistry with quarterback Malik Willis combined with Miami's overall lack of playmakers outside of De'Von Achane bodes well for the first-year receiver's prospects moving forward.

items.headline: Dulcich did not record a target across his two preseason games.
items.summary: Dulcich played a total of 15 offensive snaps across those two games before sitting for the Dolphins' preseason finale against the Falcons on Friday. Entering his sixth NFL season, the UCLA product has an opportunity to be a featured part in the Dolphins' offense due to the lack of notable skill position players outside of running back De'Von Achane. The veteran tight end also demonstrated a strong rapport with quarterback Malik Willis in training camp, setting up Dulcich to be a go-to target in the passing game for the upcoming season. Dulcich's most productive season came in his rookie campaign with the Broncos in 2022, when he caught 33 passes (on 55 targets) for 411 yards and two touchdowns across 10 regular-season games.

items.headline: Gordon (ribs) is not listed on Wednesday's injury report, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: Gordon recently returned to practice without a non-contact jersey. With his full participation in Wednesday's practice, all signs are pointing toward his availability for Week 1 versus the Raiders. The 22-year-old finished the 2025 campaign by rushing for 199 yards and three touchdowns off 70 carries, adding seven grabs for 32 yards and a touchdown in 17 regular-season appearances. Gordon currently occupies the No. 3 spot on the depth chart behind De'Von Achane and Jaylen Wright.

items.headline: Joly (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
items.summary: Joly will sit behind Greg Dulcich, Will Kacmarek and Seydou Traore. The No. 4 option at tight end will likely find himself the odd man out frequently throughout the season as he acclimates to the NFL in his first year.

items.headline: Kacmarek (calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
items.summary: The rookie third-round pick upgraded to full practice participation Friday after being limited earlier in the week. Greg Dulcich is Miami's top receiving threat at tight end, but Kacmarek could play a lot of snaps as a blocker and see a few targets here and there.

items.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed Tuesday that McCord will begin the season as the team's No. 2 quarterback, Joe Schad of The Palm Beach Post reports.
items.summary: Miami bolstered its quarterback room by claiming Brady Cook off waivers Monday, but he'll occupy the third spot on the depth chart while McCord serves as the top backup to Malik Willis. Acquired from the Packers over the weekend in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick, McCord is coming off an impressive preseason in which he completed 46 of 70 pass attempts (65.7 percent) for 446 yards and a 4:0 TD:INT over three games. The 23-year-old is still waiting to make his NFL debut, as he spent all of last season on the Eagles' practice squad after failing to make the roster as a rookie sixth-round pick.

items.headline: Tolbert (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
items.summary: With many unproven wide recievers on the roster, Tolbert will take a backseat to the trio of rookies consisting of Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell and Kevin Coleman. The fifth-year veteran will likely only get a shot at suiting up if the youth do not show enough promise over the next couple of games.

items.headline: Washington brought in three of eight targets for 53 yards, returned three kickoffs for 56 yards and ran back one punt for 17 yards in the Dolphins' 27-13 loss to the Raiders on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Washington's turnover was the one blemish on an otherwise encouraging afternoon, coming at the two-minute warning after a 26-yard reception and snuffing out any last-gasp chance at a comeback for Miami. Washington also finished as the team leader in targets and second in receiving yards for the Dolphins, and he matched Caleb Douglas for a team-high 30-yard catch. The 2024 sixth-round pick also put in solid work as a returner, and he should remain heavily involved on both offense and special teams in a Week 2 road matchup against the 49ers.

items.headline: The Dolphins signed Hunter to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Dolphins waived Hunter during Sunday's cut-down day. The running back cleared waivers and joined the practice squad in his new home. Hunter was traded to the Dolphins from the Rams last Thursday but surprisingly did not make the team's initial 53-man roster. The 23-year-old sticking around in Miami likely means the team has given him a path to potential playing time.

items.headline: The Dolphins signed Reagor to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Dolphins released Reagor during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver became a free agent and chose to sign with the team's practice squad once again. The receiving corps, consisting of Malik Washington, Jalen Tolbert, Caleb Douglas, Chris Bell, Kevin Coleman and Ryan Miller is wide open, and Reagor could prove himself worthy of a 53-man roster spot at any point throughout the 2026 season.

items.headline: The Dolphins signed Sheppard to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: The Packers waived Sheppard on Sunday. The wide receiver cleared waivers and quickly found a job with the Dolphins. Sheppard played in all three preseason contests for the Packers, catching nine balls for 81 yards and two touchdowns.

items.headline: The Dolphins signed Washington to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Dolphins waived Washington during Sunday's cut-down day. The running back cleared waivers and has rejoined the team on the practice squad. The 27-year-old participated in all three preseason contests, rushing 18 times for 41 yards.

items.headline: The Dolphins signed Watson to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: The Chiefs waived Watson during Sunday's cut-down day. The tight end cleared waivers and has found a spot with the Dolphins for the start of the regular season. The tight end participated in all three preseason games for the Chiefs, catching three of his five targets for 15 yards.

items.headline: Addison failed to record a catch on two targets in Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers.
items.summary: Addison was second on the team with his 28 routes, but his two targets were a distant fourth on the Vikings, trailing Justin Jefferson (nine), T.J. Hockenson (five) and Josh Oliver (four). Kyler Murray (concussion) was knocked out of the game in the first half, giving way to Carson Wentz, who had eyes for Jefferson and his tight ends. Addison gets a great on-paper matchup with the Bears' leaky secondary next Sunday, but the wideout will be hard to trust for fantasy lineups.

items.headline: Claiborne (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Packers, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
items.summary: Claiborne, a sixth-round selection of the Vikings in the 2026 NFL Draft, will have to wait until Week 2 against the Bears on Sunday, Sept. 20, to make his regular-season debut. With Claiborne inactive for Week 1, DeeJay Dallas will serve as the Vikings' RB3 behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason.

items.headline: The Vikings elevated Dallas from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Dallas signed with the Vikings on Sept. 2 after being released by the Jaguars during cutdown day. The running back will likely provide a special teams presence in Sunday's game against the Packers with minimal offensive usage.

items.headline: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 39-22 win over the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Justin Jefferson easily paced the Vikings with nine targets on 24 total pass attempts, but it was Hockenson who was second on the team with his five looks. His 16-yard touchdown in the third quarter pulled Minnesota within five points to make it 22-17 in favor of Green Bay. Hockenson averaged a career-low 29.2 yards per game last season, but improved quarterback play and being another year removed from ACL surgery has the veteran tight end undervalued in fantasy this season.

items.headline: Jennings played four snaps in the Vikings' 13-10 preseason win over the Giants before being held out for rest purposes in the final two exhibition tilts.
items.summary: Signed to a one-year, $8 million deal in May, Jennings is locked in as the Vikings' No. 3 receiver and didn't need to compete for a job during the preseason. With San Francisco last season, Jennings primarily operated as the "X" receiver and turned in a 55-643-9 line on 90 targets over his 15 appearances. Since Justin Jefferson typically occupies the X spot for Minnesota and Jordan Addison mainly works as the "Z" receiver, Jennings could end up seeing most of his time out of the slot with his new squad. While a slot role can often lead to catchable, higher-percentage targets, Jefferson remains the unquestioned No. 1 option in the passing game regardless of where he lines up, and Addison is capable of bumping inside and seems likely to play ahead of Jennings in two-wide formations. Moreover, Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray hasn't had an extensive track record of supporting more than one fantasy viable pass catcher during his seven-year career, so Jennings could struggle to attain consistent week-to-week volume while he's vying with the likes of Addison and tight end T.J. Hockenson for the remaining targets that don't go to Jefferson.

items.headline: Mason rushed 15 times for 59 yards and a touchdown but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 39-22 win over the Packers.
items.summary: Mason had three more carries than Aaron Jones, and neither of Minnesota's top two running backs recorded a catch. Jones and Mason each had a short touchdown run as the Vikings compiled 22 unanswered fourth-quarter points, with Mason's coming on a one-yard run with 4:48 to play. Mason set a career high with six rushing touchdowns during the 2025 regular season while rushing for 758 yards in his first year with the Vikings following a three-year stint in San Francisco. Jones and Mason are expected to split carries again in Week 2 at Chicago.

items.headline: Minnesota placed Yurosek on injured reserve Tuesday due to an undisclosed injury.
items.summary: Though the nature of Yurosek's injury isn't known, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune relays that the second-year tight end isn't expected to face a long-term absence. Yurosek will have to miss at least four games as a result of his move to IR, making the Vikings' Oct. 11 game in New Orleans as the earliest date for his potential 2026 debut. The 24-year-old mainly handled a blocking and special-teams role for the Vikings in 2025, recording just two catches for 14 yards on three targets over 12 games.

items.headline: The Vikings signed Bell to the practice squad Wednesday, Rob Kleifield reports.
items.summary: Bell made the Vikings' initial 53-man roster but was promptly waived Monday to make room for waiver claims. The wide receiver cleared waivers himself and has now returned to the team on the practice squad. The undrafted free agent out of Georgia will compete with other practice squad additions to receive a potential elevation to the active roster during the 2026 season if any starting wide receivers must miss time due to injury.

items.headline: The Vikings signed  Briscoe to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Vikings waived Briscoe during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and managed to produce enough in training camp to receive an invitation to the team's practice squad. The undrafted free agent out of Cal Poly participated in all three preseason games for the Vikings, catching one of his four targets for 11 yards.

items.headline: The Vikings signed Brosmer to the practice squad Wednesday, Rob Kleifield reports.
items.summary: Brosmer made the Vikings' initial 53-man roster before being waived on Monday. The quarterback cleared waivers and will now serve as additional depth to Kyler Murray, J.J. McCarthy (ankle) and Carson Wentz on the practice squad instead of the active roster.

items.headline: The Vikings signed Grandy to the practice squad Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Bengals waived Grandy during Sunday's cutdown day. The tight end cleared waivers and has found a new home in Minnesota. The 26-year-old participated in all three preseason games for the Bengals but was unable to catch his sole target.

items.headline: The Vikings signed  Briscoe to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Rudolph was waived by the Vikings during Sunday's cut-down day and has cleared waivers. The undrafted free agent out of Toledo impressed enough throughout training camp to earn a spot with the team's practice squad. Rudolph participated in all three preseason games but did not record any stats in the box score.

items.headline: Chism (coach's decision) is inactive for Wednesday's game against the Seahawks.
items.summary: The undrafted wide receiver out of Eastern Washington cracked the Patriots' 53-man roster after training camp for the second year in a row. He'll be a healthy scratch for the regular-season opener, and his next chance to see playing time is Week 2 against the Steelers on Sunday, Sept. 20. The Patriots will have five active wide receivers for Week 1, a group headlined by A.J. Brown, Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas.

items.headline: Doubs failed to bring in any of his three targets during the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks on Wednesday.
items.summary: The veteran offseason addition had a highly inauspicious debut, despite the fact he'd frequently impressed this summer and the Patriots lost A.J. Brown to an ankle injury on the first possession of the second half. Doubs was also the intended receiver on Drake Maye's first interception of the night, getting outleapt for a long pass by Nehemiah Pritchett early in the fourth quarter. Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports Brown was seen exiting the Patriots' locker room with a walking boot following Wednesday's game, so Doubs could be pressed into an elevated role for the Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday, Sept. 20, despite his poor showing.

items.headline: Douglas secured five of seven targets for 20 yards in the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks on Wednesday.
items.summary: Douglas finished tied with Rhamondre Stevenson for the team lead in receptions while also setting the pace in targets for the Patriots on the night. The speedy fourth-year pro's elevated role seemed to be largely the byproduct of A.J. Brown's exit from the game on the first possession of the second half due to an ankle injury, which underscores the fact Douglas' week-to-week production is likely to remain volatile over the course of the season. However, if Brown, who Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports left the locker room wearing a walking boot Wednesday, misses any time, Douglas would be in line for additional snaps and targets.

items.headline: Hollins secured four of five targets for 51 yards in the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks on Wednesday.
items.summary: The veteran wideout was listed as No. 4 on the depth chart heading into the season opener, but Hollins finished as the team leader in receiving yards on the night. Hollins also had a team-high 19-yard reception, and he became much more of a factor after A.J. Brown went down early in the third quarter with an ankle injury. Brown exited the locker room donning a walking boot per Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald, so Hollins could be tasked with an elevated role again in the Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: Kiner turned six carries into 11 yards during Wednesday night's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Kiner operated as the Patriots' No. 2 running back behind starter Rhamondre Stevenson with TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) unavailable. Kiner was on the field for eight of the team's 71 total offensive snaps, with Stevenson (60) handling the lion's share. If Henderson is sidelined again in Week 2, Kiner will likely operate in a similar role against the Steelers.

items.headline: Larison reverted to New England's practice squad Thursday, per the NFL's transaction log.
items.summary: Larison was elevated for Wednesday's season-opening loss to Seattle and logged three offensive snaps, catching both of his targets for nine yards. The 24-year-old also returned two kickoffs for 49 yards. Larison's opportunity came as a result of TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) missing Wednesday's contest, and Henderson's status for Week 2 will likely factor into Larison's likelihood of being elevated for that game. Even if Larison gets elevated again, though, he'll likely continue to work behind Rhamondre Stevenson (60 snaps Wednesday) and Corey Kiner (eight).

items.headline: The Patriots claimed Latu off waivers Monday.
items.summary: The Eagles waived Latu on Sunday, but the tight end will not become a free agent. With Julian Hill (knee) done for the season, the Patriots needed additional depth at tight end behind Hunter Henry. The team released K.J. Britt in a corresponding move.

items.headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback for Wednesday's game against the Seahawks.
items.summary: As the emergency third quarterback, Morton is prohibited from seeing the field Wednesday unless Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito are both removed from the contest due to injury, illness or ejection. Morton was a seventh-round selection of the Patriots in the 2026 NFL Draft and played in all three preseason games, completing 38 of 58 passes (65.5 percent) for 318 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions while turning four carries into 18 yards.

items.headline: Raridon caught his only target for a two-yard touchdown in Wednesday's 13-10 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Raridon opened the scoring in the second quarter with a two-yard touchdown catch on his first career target, but the Patriots failed to hold onto the lead. The rookie third-round pick out of Notre Dame played 38 of the team's 71 snaps on offense, and Raridon is the clear No. 2 tight end behind Hunter Henry, who caught all three of his targets Wednesday.

items.headline: Stevenson rushed 18 times for 51 yards and brought in five of six targets for 44 yards in the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks on Wednesday.
items.summary: As expected with TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) unavailable, Stevenson shouldered a heavy workload and found running room at a premium save for his game-long 12-yard rush late in the fourth quarter. However, the versatile veteran made an impact as a receiver, finishing with a co-team-high reception total while checking in as the runner-up in both receiving yards and targets for the Patriots on the night. Stevenson's involvement as a pass catcher unsurprisingly picked up after A.J. Brown went down with an ankle injury on the first possession of the second half, and the veteran running back could remain in an elevated all-around role during the Week 2 home opener against the Steelers on Sunday, Sept. 20.

items.headline: Williams wasn't targeted in the Patriots' 13-10 loss to the Seahawks on Wednesday night.
items.summary: Williams played 12 of 71 offensive snaps and ran just seven routes on 36 dropbacks by Drake Maye. He played another four snaps on special teams, returning a pair of kicks for 58 yards. With A.J. Brown (ankle) now looking at an extended absence, Williams should see a bigger role on offense behind Romeo Doubs over the next few weeks. The big-play threat will be a name to watch on the waiver wire in fantasy but isn't someone worth adding outside of deep leagues at the moment.

items.headline: The Patriots signed  Dixon to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Patriots waived Dixon last Saturday in preparation for last Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and has returned to the team on the practice squad. The undrafted free agent out of Culver-Stockton played in the final two preseason games for the Patriots, catching all 10 of his targets for 81 yards.

items.headline: The Patriots signed  Dorner to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Patriots waived Dorner last Saturday in anticipation of last Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and has chosen to stay with the team on the practice squad. The undrafted free agent out of North Texas participated in all three preseason games, catching four of his five targets for 37 yards.

items.headline: The Patriots signed  Haskins to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Patriots cut Haskins last Saturday in anticipation of Sunday's cutdown day. The running back rejoined the team Monday and will compete with Lan Larison for the primary running back role with the practice squad. Haskins participated in all three preseason games, rushing 20 times for 69 yards.

items.headline: The Patriots signed Zylstra to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: The Bills cut Zylstra last Saturday. The tight end now joins up with the team's main divisional rival in the race for the AFC East title. The 29-year-old has played in 35 career regular-season games with the Lions, catching 18 balls for 136 yards and four touchdowns.

items.headline: The Saints have elevated Austin from the practice squad to the active roster ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
items.summary: Austin signed with the Saints' practice squad Sept. 2 after being waived by the team on cutdown day. The wide receiver will likely see minimal targets, as he is set to be the fifth option. If Austin does see the field, the majority of his snaps will likely occur on special teams.

items.headline: Delp (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions.
items.summary: Delp didn't practice at all this week after initially suffering the injury last month. The third-round rookie will have to wait to make his regular-season debut. Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant will handle tight-end duties for New Orleans.

items.headline: The Saints have elevated Donaldson from the practice squad to the active roster ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
items.summary: Donaldson signed with the Saints' practice squad Sept. 2 after being a casualty of the team's Aug. 30 cuts. The running back will fill in for Audric Estime (thigh) as a reserve option behind Travis Etienne, Alvin Kamara (knee), and Kendre Miller while Estime recovers from his thigh issue on IR.

items.headline: Fant caught four of his eight targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions.
items.summary: Tyler Shough enjoyed targeting tight ends in Sunday's shootout, with the duo of Fant and Juwan Johnson totalling 87 yards and two touchdowns between them. If Shough's favoritism for the bigger-bodied targets with a higher catch radius continues, Fant could become a solid option in deeper leagues.

items.headline: Olave caught 10 of 13 targets for 182 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions.
items.summary: As expected, Olave was Tyler Shough's top downfield option, but there was plenty of volume to go around as the second-year QB aired it out 56 times as the Saints mounted a big second-half comeback to force OT. Olave was forced to leave the field at one point due to calf cramping, per Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com, but the issue wasn't serious. The fifth-year wideout will continue to march toward his fourth career 1,000-yard campaign in Week 2 on the road against the Ravens.

items.headline: The Saints signed Welch to the active roster from the practice squad Saturday, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
items.summary: With Audric Estime (thigh) moved to IR in a surprise move, the Saints gained an open spot on the 53-man roster. Welch will be the No. 3 tight end due to Oscar Delp (hamstring) being ruled out and will likely participate almost exclusively on special teams and in 13-personnel sets, if he plays at all in the team's Week 1 matchup with the Lions.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Lions.
items.summary: Spencer Rattler kept his gig as the QB2 behind Tyler Shough this summer, leaving Wilson as the emergency option entering the season. Wilson appeared in four games with the Dolphins last season, completing six of 11 passes for 32 yards.

items.headline: The Saints placed Estime (thigh) on injured reserve Saturday, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
items.summary: Estime was ruled out for Sunday's game against Detroit with a thigh injury. The running back's injury came out of nowhere but movement to IR likely means it is a significant issue. Estime will need to miss the first four games of the regular season before he is eligible to return to the field.

items.headline: Tipton (leg) was moved to the reserve/PUP list by the Saints on Sunday.
items.summary: Tipton underwent tibia surgery in the offseason, and as a result, he opened training camp on the active/PUP list, ultimately failing to play during the preseason. The wide receiver will now be forced to miss at least four contests to open the regular season, and the earliest he'd be able to return to action is Week 5 versus the Vikings on Oct. 11.

items.headline: New Orleans signed Moreno-Cropper to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Moreno-Cropper went unclaimed on waivers after the Saints cut him Sunday, and now he's back with the organization as a member of the practice squad. In three games with the Cowboys in 2025, he did not draw any targets, but he did contribute returning punts and kicks.

items.headline: The Saints signed Palmer to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: The Saints waived Palmer during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and will rejoin his 2025 team on the practice squad. Palmer was claimed by the Saints in August of 2025 but never played in a regular-season game for the franchise due to multiple injuries.

items.headline: Rowan was signed to the practice squad with New Orleans on Tuesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: Rowan was waived by the Broncos on Aug. 29 and he ultimately went unclaimed on the open market. He will now get an opportunity to prove himself with the Saints as an additional depth option for the team at wide receiver ahead of the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: The Saints signed Smartt to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: The Eagles released Smartt on Saturday. The tight end will provide additional depth to the tight ends on the 53-man roster. If rookie third-rounder Oscar Delp (hamstring) is held out of the Saints' Week 1 matchup against the Lions, Smartt could be elevated to the active roster immediately.

items.headline: The Saints signed Tillman to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: The Browns waived Tillman last Thursday because he was dealing with an undisclosed injury. The 26-year-old was a valuable depth piece for the team, but with multiple rookie wide receivers, the 2023 third-rounder was no longer needed. Tillman cleared waivers and a medical exam, and will now provide additional receiver depth to the Saints.

items.headline: New Orleans signed White to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: White was released Sunday after missing the cut for the Saints' initial 53-man roster, but they brought him back to fill a spot on the practice squad. With Alvin Kamara (knee) and Kendre Miller (undisclosed) both tending to injuries, White could potentially end up being a candidate for elevation as early as Week 1.

items.headline: Odell Beckham Jr. reclaims iconic No. 13 jersey with Giants
items.summary: The star wide receiver is returning to the number he wore during his first stint in New York from 2014 to 2018.

items.headline: The Giants signed Cambre to a contract Saturday, Art Stapleton of The Bergen Record reports.
items.summary: The Giants waived Cambre during cutdown day before signing the wide receiver to the practice squad Sept. 2. The second-year player out of Louisiana will likely be a reserve option if Malik Nabers (knee) has not quite recovered enough from his 2025 ACL tear to suit up.

items.headline: Fields appears on track to open the season as the Giants' No. 2 wide receiver after the team released Darius Slayton on Monday, Matt Iegros of USA Today reports.
items.summary: Prior to his release, Slayton looked like the leading candidate to handle the perimeter role opposite Malik Nabers (knee). Those duties instead could fall to Fields, a third-round rookie out of Notre Dame. Listed at 6-foot-4 and 222 pounds, Fields drew positive buzz in training camp and the preseason for his physicality and ability to make plays downfield. The Giants still have veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham on hand to push for playing time, but Fields often took reps ahead of both players while Nabers was sidelined or limited to non-contact portions of practice for much of camp.

items.headline: Harris (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Harris signed with the Giants in mid-August to add depth to the backfield. He'll be a healthy scratch for Week 1, while the Giants roll with three active running backs in Cam Skattebo, Tyrone Tracy and veteran Devin Singletary. Harris' next chance to suit up is Week 2 against the Rams on Monday, Sept. 21.

items.headline: Johnson (shoulder) was a full practice participant Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Johnson is coming off a 2025 regular season in which he posted a 45-528-5 line on 74 targets in 15 games, but the arrival of TE Isaiah Likely via free agency has provided the former with some competition at the position ahead of his third pro campaign. With the shoulder injury he picked up in an Aug. 24 practice behind Johnson, he'll focus on being a regular part of the Giants offense in Sunday's Week 1 matchup with the Cowboys.

items.headline: Devin Singletary flies into end zone untouched to pad Giants' lead
items.summary: Devin Singletary flies into end zone untouched to pad Giants' lead

items.headline: Tracy (neck) wasn't listed on the Giants' first Week 1 injury report Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Tracy sustained an apparent neck injury during New York's exhibition finale, but after landing a spot on the team's initial active roster and having nearly two weeks to recover, he's in good health ahead of a Week 1 matchup with the Cowboys. With Cam Skattebo leading the Giants backfield and Najee Harris and Devin Singletary also on hand for reps, it remains to be seen what kind of workload Tracy can expect in the regular-season opener.

items.headline: The Giants signed Hyatt to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Hyatt was part of the Giants' 53-man roster cuts over the weekend but will stick around after passing through waivers unclaimed. A third-round pick in 2023, Hyatt has just 36 career regular-season catches for 470 yards and zero touchdowns across 41 appearances. Odell Beckham beat Hyatt out for a roster spot this summer.

items.headline: The Giants signed Jones to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: The Bengals waived Jones during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and will now move to New York to begin the regular season. Jones competed to be the Bengals' primary return specialist but lost out on the job to Ke'Shawn Williams and Samaje Perine. The 27-year-old will now provide additional depth to the Giants from the practice squad.

items.headline: Allen is listed second on the Jets' unofficial depth chart behind Breece Hall.
items.summary: Allen worked with the starters for most of the preseason while Hall was sidelined by a groin injury. Hall practiced without limitations Wednesday, as did Isaiah Davis (knee), who is listed third on the team's unofficial depth chart. Allen is listed at 235 pounds and has reportedly bulked up to around 250. The 2024 fourth-round pick's large frame could help Allen command valuable goal-line and short-yardage work even while Hall is healthy.

items.headline: Davis (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Davis missed training camp practices and preseason games while recovering from a knee injury, but his full participation in Wednesday's session indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's regular-season opener against the Titans. The third-year pro projects to serve as the Jets' RB3 this season behind Breece Hall and Braelon Allen.

items.headline: Nwangwu (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans.
items.summary: Nwangwu was designated as doubtful after Friday's practice, so the eventual ruling that he will not suit up for Sunday's contest is not surprising. The depth running back and primary kick returner for the team continues to deal with a back injury he likely suffered during a practice session earlier in the week. With Nwangwu out, wide receiver Isaiah Williams will likely add kick return duties alongside his punt return duties in Sunday's game.

items.headline: Taylor is listed as a starting tight end on the Jets' initial depth chart ahead of a Week 1 game against the Titans.
items.summary: New York listed both Taylor and Jeremy Ruckert as starters at tight end, notably omitting first-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq (abdomen) after he missed most of the summer recovering from hernia surgery. Sadiq is on track to play Week 1 against Tennessee, but he's going to have to earn his spot over Taylor and Ruckert. Taylor fits the mold more as a traditional in-line Y tight end, while Sadiq profiles more as an F tight end, functioning as a big slot receiver. Taylor could be a factor in the red zone this season.

items.headline: Week 1 winners and losers: Caleb Williams and Josh Allen dominate; Ja'Marr Chase disappoints
items.summary: Caleb Williams, Josh Allen and Trevor Lawrence came up big in Week 1, while Ja'Marr Chase, Drake London and Colston Loveland had very quiet days.

items.headline: The Jets placed Patrick (groin) on injured reserve Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Patrick was ruled out ahead of Sunday's contest after Friday's practice. The wide receiver's groin injury seems to be lingering, so the 32-year-old will spend some time on IR. Patrick will be eligible to return from IR after four games, meaning Isaiah Williams and Arian Smith will likely see a greater share of reserve opportunities with the Jets' wide receiver corps.

items.headline: Trayanum (neck) was placed on injured reserve by the Jets on Sunday, Eric Allen & Amanda Vogt of the team's official website report.
items.summary: Trayanum suffered a neck injury in the team's preseason finale against the Giants on Friday. The running back is now set to miss the entire 2026 campaign while on IR with New York, and he'd have to reach an injury settlement with the team to have a chance to play this season.

items.headline: The Jets signed McClain to the practice squad Monday, Eric Allen and Amanda Vogt of the team's official site report.
items.summary: The Jets waived McClain during Sunday's cut-down day. The undrafted free agent out of Arizona State cleared waivers and now rejoins the team that took a shot on him in early May. McClain played in all three preseason games, catching three of his six targets for 33 yards.

items.headline: The Jets signed Pritchett to the practice squad Monday, Eric Allen and Amanda Vogt of the team's official site report.
items.summary: The Jets waived Pritchett during Sunday's cut-down day. The wide receiver cleared waivers and has once again earned a practice squad role similar to the one he had during the 2025 season. The second-year player out of South Alabama was not elevated to the active roster for any games in 2025 and is still waiting to appear in his first NFL regular-season game.

items.headline: The Jets signed Zappe to the practice squad Tuesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The Jets cut Zappe last Saturday. The quarterback was competing for the No. 2 role behind Geno Smith but lost out to Cade Klubnik and Brady Cook. Zappe will now provide additional depth at the position and be ready to be elevated as an emergency quarterback if any of the first three options must miss time due to injury.

items.headline: Bigsby played 10 offensive snaps this preseason before being rested for the final two exhibition contests.
items.summary: The fact he was rested for Weeks 2 and 3 of the preseason while Will Shipley played would suggest Bigsby has a firm grip on RB2 duties in Philadelphia behind Saquon Barkley. Barkley is entering his age-29 season with plenty of miles on his proverbial tires, and there's been talk out of Philly that the team wants to get Bigsby more involved to keep Barkley fresh. If something were to happen to him injury-wise, Bigsby would immediately enter the fantasy RB1 conversation in the Eagles' run-heavy offense that features one of the league's best offensive lines, making him the premier bench stash headed into the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: The Eagles elevated Covey from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: With the entirety of the Eagles' wide receiver corps healthy, Covey was likely elevated for his value on special teams. There is a good chance Covey takes punt and kick return reps away from Makai Lemon and Will Shipley, keeping the wide receiver and running back fresh for offensive possessions.

items.headline: McKee (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
items.summary: McKee will be the emergency option behind Jalen Hurts and Andy Dalton. The quarterback will only enter the game if both active players are unable to play.

items.headline: Moore (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
items.summary: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown are set to be the starting four wide receivers for the Eagles in Week 1. Moore is the odd man out, set to likely be inactive until another player wastes his chance or gets injured.

items.headline: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
